item.title: Sony has announced next month’s PS Plus offerings, dropping on November 3. If you’re into killing zombies, roguelite card games, or delving into ancient tombs, you’re in for a treat.
item.description:
Sony has announced next month’s PS Plus offerings, dropping on November 3. If you’re into killing zombies, roguelite card games, or delving into ancient tombs, you’re in for a treat.
Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV, V, and VI Remastered, and Monster Train 2 are joining the PS Plus library.
Dead Island 2 takes place in a sun-drenched Los Angeles (it isn’t an island, but don’t worry about it) overtaken by hordes of undead. You use modded weapons to slice and smack your way to safety, taking in the bloody and brilliantly layered gore system as you go.
Dead Island 2 - 10 Disgusting Ways To Tear Zombies Apart
There’s also the Tomb Raider Darkness trilogy, which is composed of Tomb Raider: The Last Revelation, Tomb Raider: Chronicles and Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness. These remasters let you switch between the original polygonal graphics and remastered look at will.
Monster Train 2 is a treat for anyone who loves Slay the Spire. Instead of blending card games with RPG-style combat, this sees you use cards to hold enemies off on a moving train, mixing tower defense elements into the recipe. Just one more run. One more. I promise.
The games are all available to redeem from Tuesday November 3 to Monday, November 30. In the meantime, you have until November 2 to redeem last month’s games.
Last month’s PS Plus games were F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896, and Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2. F1 25 is obviously good if you’re a fan of the sport, but the secret best game there is Hunt: Showdown 1896.
Hunt: Showdown is an extraction shooter like no other, where stealth and noise generation are more important than your aim — though that’s also important because you’re rocking old-school Western weapons that take time to reload. It’s deep and brilliant and deserves a way bigger playerbase, especially after its latest updates.
You can browse the PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium Game Catalog on our dedicated page.

item.title: Just as No Man’s Sky lands for iOS, the ever-expanding space sim is getting a spooky new update in time for Halloween.
item.description:
Just as No Man’s Sky lands for iOS, the ever-expanding space sim is getting a spooky new update in time for Halloween. Forsaken is the latest from Hello Games, which redeemed itself for No Man’s Sky’s poor launch years ago but just keeps going with massive free updates anyway.
Last month, the developer released the No Man’s Sky Cosmos update in time for the game’s tenth anniversary. Cosmos made space more exciting to explore, letting you get close to stars, build your own space station, and explore the wreckage of huge space hulks.
Forsaken aims to show the “darker side of the universe,” according to Hello Games. You’ll be able to search the universe for haunted technology and biological horrors to sell to eccentric traders, but to get them you’ll have to brave the most harrowing corners of the cosmos.
No Man's Sky Forsaken Screenshots
Trading the items grants new seasonal items, including “creepy and organic” shipbuilding options, from alien cockpits to unknowable modules. There are also new cosmetics for your character, from larva tank helmets to writhing, wormy multi-tools. Yummy.
On top of the seasonal stuff, there are also UI tweaks like a better radial menu, a minimal HUD option, and a bunch of other quality of life and accessibility options to tinker with. One of the coolest additions lets you warp straight to any star you can see from your cockpit.
The Forsaken update is available today on all platforms, including the newly minted No Man’s Sky for iOS. Check out the full patch notes on the No Man’s Sky website.
If you’re wondering why Hello Games just keeps going with No Man’s Sky — other than its massive popularity — just look at its upcoming game, Light No Fire. Light No Fire is a sword and sorcery RPG from the team that, instead of simulating an endless galaxy, simulates a more densely packed, to scale planet. An entire planet.
A lot of the updates and tweaks to No Man’s Sky are technical advances Hello Games is using to develop Light No Fire, which will let you soar across the skies on dragonback. We haven’t seen Light No Fire since The Game Awards 2023.
After the sketchy launch of No Man’s Sky, it seems like the Hello Games team plans to let the game speak for itself this time around.

item.title: Back when housing was added to World of Warcraft at the beginning of Midnight, Blizzard issued a set of guiding priciples that, among other things, promised that the company wouldn't add cosmetics to the cash store that represent one of Azeroth's races or classes. This week, Blizzard broke that promise.
item.description:
Back when housing was added to World of Warcraft at the beginning of Midnight, Blizzard issued a set of guiding priciples that, among other things, promised that the company wouldn't add cosmetics to the cash store that represent one of Azeroth's races or classes. This week, Blizzard broke that promise.
Blizzard released two housing packs yesterday: the Haunted Grimtide Estate pack with a housing exterior and a pre-built interior, along with the Grimtide Decor Pack, which includes 21 different decorations that you can fill that interior with. The company is charging 2,500 hearthsteel for the Haunted Grimtide Estate pack and 1,000 hearthsteel for the Decor Pack, or $25 and $10, respectively.
It would make sense to have a spooky decor pack ahead of Halloween, but the aesthetics of all of these items looks like they were ripped right from Stormsong Valley and the Kul'Tiran humans that debuted in Battle for Azeroth. And the problem there is that charging for packs that so directly reference a WoW race and zone goes directly against the guiding principles that Blizzard itself published when it released housing.
World of Warcraft: Midnight Cinematic Images and First Screenshots
Understandably, a lot of players are upset about these housing packs. One of the biggest WoW influencers, BellularGaming, tweeted a screenshot of Blizzard's promise, adding, "Kul'tiran housing decor bundle in the store! Ever wondered why I dgaf about having a professional relationship with Blizzard anymore? When their words mean nothing, Interviews are a waste of time."
In his replies, user LucasMillican begged players not to buy the items, saying, "Call it out, keep calling it out. Hold them accountable for their words. And for the love of god, people, don’t spend money on it. If you buy it, that tells them it’s okay. Don’t f***ing buy it."
Over on Reddit, WoW fans are rallying around a WindowsCentral article calling out the decor packs, in a thread that has over 660 replies at the time of writing.
User AliceLunar said: "And now here we are, still paying a monthly fee, buying new expansions every other year.. But now we have a whole cash shop, $90 mounts, $75 tree houses, pets, skins, built in RMT, new race locked behind a $30 paywall and the list goes on. WoW has more greedy and insane monetization than a F2P MMO from 20 years ago, but it's not free to play, and people keep opening their wallet."
Another user, Tiroler_Manu, wanted Blizzard to admit it was wrong, saying, "Just openly say: 'Yeah it was a greedy f**k up move, we violated our own principles, we won't do it again, we will give all players this and former house costumizations for free and refund purchases of House customizations. House customizations from now on will not be buyable, except special (non racial) collaborations for charity events (where of course the money will go to the charity).'"
The World of Warcraft cash shop has grown considerably over the last few years, and hasn't shown any signs of slowing down. I'm not sure if community pushback is going to do much for this specific pack, but hopefully there's a chance that it'll dissuade Blizzard from charging for other housing items that so clearly reference the races and classes that players identify with.
This controversy is coming to one of the most popular additions to World of Warcraft in years. When Midnight first launched, housing blew up so much that players (myself included) rushed to collect a ton of housing items to create their Azerothian home. It was so popular, in fact, that Zillow even added a page to show off players' homes.
World of Warcraft Forever or Retail?

item.title: Nintendo’s Indie World Showcase is over, and we’ve got a roundup of all the announcements right here.
item.description:
Nintendo’s Indie World Showcase is over, and we’ve got a roundup of all the announcements right here!
Witchbrook release date
Indie World Showcase kicked off with a big announcement: Chucklefish's Witchbrook finally has a release date! The hotly anticipated magical life sim is coming in to PC, Nintendo Switch 1 and 2, and Xbox on January 28, 2027. There's a new gameplay trailer, too. That's not all. Outside of Indie World Showcase, Chucklefish confirmed plans for a PlayStation 5 port.
Here's the official blurb:
Winds of Viridia demo
Winds of Viridia, from Shark Jump, is due out early 2027, with a free demo available from the eShop today.
City of None reveal
City of None is a new indie game coming from one of the co-creators of the much-loved Celeste. It's due out next year. Here's the official blurb from Nintendo:
Sword of the Sea is coming to Nintendo Switch 2
Giant Squid's 2025 adventure video game Sword of the Sea is coming to Switch 2 on October 29.
Tenjutsu Switch 2 confirmed
The lead designer of Dead Cells has a new game, Tenjutsu, which is now confirmed for Nintendo Switch 2. Dead Cells designer Sébastien Benard’s fast-paced, full-blooded action roguelike is coming to Switch 2 alongside PC in 2027, and we've got a new gameplay trailer.
Riyo Games and Balor Games’ turn-based RPG Threads of Time has a summer 2027 launch on Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PC via Steam, and Xbox Series X and S. The Switch versions were also revealed today during Nintendo’s Indie World showcase.
Dumpster Gang from Curve Games and Coyote House Games is a chaotic online sandbox that charges players with solving puzzles and stealing everything they can carry as a trash panda. It's due out on Switch 2 next March.
Super Battle Golf
Super Battle Golf lets up to eight players battle in chaotic golf games. It's due out on Switch 2 on March 25, 2027.
semiwork's viral viral online co-op extraction horror game R.E.P.O. is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027. It launched on Steam in early access form last year and blew up.
Haunted Paws from LazyFlock is a two-player cosy adventure where you play as a puppy. It's due out next May, with a free demo available on the eShop later today.
Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino
We have a new trailer for Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino, from Japanese developer Rias. Kitsune is a fox girl who finds herself on Adashino Island and starts travelling with her Frog friend. Neon signs give light and color to the island with a Japanese-inspired atmosphere. It comes out spring 2027.
Monomi Park's Slime Rancher 2 launches on Switch 2 in January 2027.
Spirit Crossing, from from Spry Fox, launches as a console exclusive on Switch 1 and 2 on November 16.
My Arms Are Longer Now
My Arms Are Longer Now from Toot Games and Jackbox Games is a physics-based heist game where you play a really long arm. Yes, really. It's developed by an Australian indie developer and features voice acting from actual Australian comedians. It's due out March 11, 2027.
Switch 2 console exclusive Petal Runner, from Nano Park Studios, has a release date: March 8, 2027. There's a demo going live on the eShop today, too.
Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition
Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition, from Playstack and Doraccoon, launches on Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, alongside an exclusive in-game arcade cabinet skin. Preorders and a free demo go live on the eShop later today.

item.title: Massive Entertainment has announced that The Division series has recorded over 50 million players across its games, just as the series hits its 10th anniversary. That’s a lot of +1 defense beanies!
item.description:
Massive Entertainment has announced that The Division series has recorded over 50 million players across its games, just as the series hits its 10th anniversary. That’s a lot of +1 defense beanies!
The long-running looter shooter began life in 2016 with the launch of The Division. It came out three years after its flashy reveal at Ubisoft's E3 2013 conference which, at the time, exceeded expectation for next-gen gaming (remember when the guy closed the car door while in cover?). The Division 2 followed in 2019, but sales failed to meet Ubisoft's expectations. A number of spinoffs have come and gone since.
Massive Entertainment announced a new DLC for The Division 2 at a community panel at Gamescom earlier this year. The Echoes of Central Park DLC releases on November 3. It seems likely the new expansion — which adds a horror-themed flashback campaign, a stash space increase, a level boost, and more — will see even more players shoot numbers out of some guys across the U.S., both returning and new.
With those kinds of numbers, it’s no surprise Ubisoft and Massive aren’t done with the series. Tom Clancy's The Division 3 is also officially in production at Massive Entertainment. Originally headed up by executive producer Julian Gerighty (who also led Star Wars Outlaws and The Division 2), The Division 3 is now in the hands of creative director Mathias Karlson, game director on The Division 2. Gerighty recently left Ubisoft to work at Battlefield developer DICE.
Gerighty confirmed his departure in a social media post just a week after appearing on a livestream to promote The Division 3. “So, The Division 3 is in production, right?” he said before his departure. “This is not a secret. It's been announced. It's shaping up to be a monster.
“I can't really say anything more than that. But this is, within these walls in Massive, we are working extremely hard on something that I think will be as big an impact as Division 1 was.”
Tom Clancy’s The Division 2 Echoes of Central Park DLC Screenshots
Following his departure, Massive reassured fans that The Division 3 was in safe hands. “For our players, don’t worry, Agents,” the studio said in a social media post. “Our teams who built this world with Julian are still here, carrying it forward with an ambitious, unchanged commitment to the future.”
There’s no word on when The Division 3 will launch, but Ubisoft is making it a priority. Late last year, Massive Entertainment introduced what it called a "voluntary career transition program," as part of a move to focus on The Division franchise and its Snowdrop game engine.

item.title: Valve’s Steam Business Team took to the stage at the Steam Indie Connect event in Korea and took questions from an audience of game developers. During the chat, the issue of Steam being flooded with generative AI slop games and knockoff AI clones came up, and Valve said it’s still trying to figure out how to navigate this new world.
item.description:
Valve’s Steam Business Team took to the stage at the Steam Indie Connect event in Korea and took questions from an audience of game developers. During the chat, the issue of Steam being flooded with generative AI slop games and knockoff AI clones came up, and Valve said it’s still trying to figure out how to navigate this new world.
Last year, roughly 17% of Steam Next Fest demos disclosed the use of generative AI, and this year was likely higher as the platform hosted over 8,000 demos during the event. It’s a huge discoverability problem for developers who’ve poured years of their lives into their games, only to get swept up in the slop deluge.
Then there are the AI clones, which are becoming a growing issue. Developers are becoming more and more concerned about showing off their games, as bad actors are using generative AI to clone them from early footage and demos, beating them to the market with a bad copy.
Steam Machine – Hands On Photos
During Steam Indie Connect, Valve’s Tom Giardino addressed concerns around clones, noting that they existed before AI and have only accelerated the process. "We don't want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn't use," he said (thanks, InvaGlobal), ruling out Valve outright banning developers who do this.
"Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective," he added, shifting the onus onto the developer of the original game.
The issue of discoverability also came up, with developers in the audience noting that it’s harder than ever to stand out among all the throwaway AI games flooding digital storefronts like Steam, but particularly during Next Fest where developers are looking to find their audience ahead of release. According to Valve’s Marc Wilkinson, it’s not as bad as it seems.
During the first two days of Next Fest, recommendations are completely random, but personalized recommendations kick in later based on user activity. Once that kicks in, players are more likely to find the games they love. Wilkinson said that articles pointing out the flood of low-quality games were based on the first couple of days, before personalized recommendations kicked in.
According to Valve, the algorithm has to be completely random at first. This is to prevent system abuse from developers figuring out how to game the algorithm.
"We recognize that the trade-off is that some low-quality games get exposed," Wilkinson said. "We are fully aware of the situation, and a significant number of people are thinking about how to solve this problem."
Giardino added, "We don't think we're perfect and there's plenty of room for improvement. Rather than limiting developer access, making Steam a smarter and more dynamic platform is the starting point of our philosophy."
Photo by Olly Curtis/Future Publishing via Getty Images.

item.title: You need to have completed Crimson Desert’s main storyline to begin Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane’s new DLC stories, Pearl Abyss has confirmed.
item.description:
You need to have completed Crimson Desert’s main storyline to begin Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane’s new DLC stories, Pearl Abyss has confirmed.
Speaking on Dropped Frames, Pearl Abyss' Will Powers confirmed two entry points for the Charting the Unknown DLC, which launches on October 29. You’ll need to have completed the main storyline to play the first entry point, which is the epilogue story content for each of the three main characters. The second is, you need to have established the Greymane camp during Chapter 3 of the main game to be able to play the new open world content, which includes exploration, naval gameplay, and pretty much everything that is not the new character-specific story DLC.
“There's storylines for the three characters,” Powers explained. “Damiane, Oongka, and Kliff, you didn't really get to explore a lot of their backstory, a lot of their motivations during the main game. Now, it's effectively an epilogue for all three characters. What are they doing after? They're not necessarily together anymore and traveling together. After all of this, what is Oongka going to do in the world? What is Damiane going to do in the world? What is Kliff going to do in the world? So there are those storylines, which are really cool and unique in and of themselves.
“But then there's also this storyline and this quest line around this new area of the map that you can play though.”
Crimson Desert Enhanced: Charting the Unknown Screenshots
While completing the main Crimson Desert storyline is no mean feat (it’s a massive game that many are still soldiering through even now!), it makes sense that any epilogue story DLC would have to have this requirement rather than be baked into the main campaign to avoid spoilers.
Indeed, Powers made this point on the show. “It would ruin the story for people that are focused on that stuff,” he said. “If you want open world content, if you want to be able to access all that stuff, you can do it very early in the game. If you want story focused content, then you've probably already beaten the story. So you'll be able to continue along that.”
Still, it's worth noting that not that many have actually completed Crimson Desert's main story, in percentage terms at least. According to official Steam achievements data, just 10.8% of all players have unlocked the Expert Storyteller achievement, which is awarded for completing all main quests. Perhaps we shouldn't be surprised by the data here; Crimson Desert is a game packed with hundreds, if not thousands of hours of content, and it is easy to get sidetracked. Personally, I've logged nearly 70 hours in Crimson Desert on Steam, but am nowhere near finishing the main story. I'm not sure I ever will.
Charting the Unknown adds new stories, ocean exploration, romance, business management and expanded housing to an already feature-packed Pywel. We have everything you need to know about the major additions in a Crimson Desert Charting the Unknown DLC features roundup.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero is on track to be a huge hit, with estimates suggesting the action game has already sold over 1 million copies before launch.
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero is on track to be a huge hit, with estimates suggesting the action game has already sold over 1 million copies before launch.
In a post on social media, Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, estimated that Phantom Blade Zero had sold 850,000 pre-launch copies on Western launch platforms Steam and PS5, with sales on Tencent’s WeGame (an online PC storefront in China) bumping the total figure above 1 million.
Of the Western launch prelaunch sales, Elliott estimated three quarters were on Steam. Nearly two thirds of total prelaunch sales are from China, Taiwan, or Hong Kong. Phantom Blade Zero is a wuxia action game developed by Chinese studio S-Game, and features martial arts movie star Donnie Yen.
Phantom Blade Zero - Donnie Yen Behind the Scenes Photos
Elliott said that Phantom Blade Zero's prelaunch sales had generated $43 million in revenue, and had cracked the top 40 games of 2026 by revenue before it’s even released, despite only being available on PC and PS5. He did, however, add that Phantom Blade Zero is unlikely to hit the sales heights of 2024's megahit, Black Myth Wukong, but still, "it'll sell a lot of copies this year in a crowded market."
For context, Game Science's Black Myth Wukong sold an eye-watering 10 million copies in the first three days alone, and has reportedly sold over 20 million copies to date. Unsurprisingly, a follow-up is in development.
IGN’s 9/10 Phantom Blade review called it “an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger.”
If you’re wondering when you can start swinging, check out our Phantom Blade Zero global release times and preload details post. There’s a full breakdown for exactly when you can fire it up for major cities around the world.
Phantom Blade Zero looks set to be one of the biggest video games of October 2026, rubbing shoulders with the likes of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, and Final Fantasy Resonance. 2026 is shaping up to be a special year, with the Ocarina of Time remake and GTA 6 still to come.

item.title: The legal battle between Nintendo and Pocketpair is ongoing, but the Palworld developer hasn’t ruled out a Switch 2 version of its creature collecting survival game.
item.description:
The legal battle between Nintendo and Pocketpair is ongoing, but the Palworld developer hasn’t ruled out a Switch 2 version of its creature collecting survival game.
Nintendo and The Pokémon Company are currently embroiled in ongoing litigation with Pocketpair in Japan, with patents that revolve around how Pokémon games work at the heart of the lawsuit. IP experts have indicated that Nintendo may only receive a $30,000 payout if it wins, but it's looking increasingly likely that Nintendo will lose.
Skirting around the elephant in the room in an interview with VGC, Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe said he’d love to get Palworld on Switch 2. “Of course,” Mizobe replied when asked if the studio had Switch 2 ambitions. “First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry.
Palworld: Palfarm First Screenshots
“It’s been an incredible platform. If there’s ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we’d love to have those conversations.”
Of course, the current legal dispute would have to play out before those conversations can happen, and that’s assuming there’s no bad blood once legal proceedings are done and dusted.
Nintendo filed a patent infringement lawsuit in September 2024, but the complaint was modified in November 2025 after Palworld updates changed some of the most egregious of the Pokemon-inspired game mechanics. One such mechanic was the ability to throw a sphere to summon a creature, which was removed in Early Access patch v0.3.11.
Now when you summon a Pal, it simply spawns directly beside your character while you hold out the sphere. This change to avoid stepping on Nintendo’s patent removed some of the tactical options the player had, since they were no longer able to summon a Pal to a specific spot to draw aggro or hit an enemy from a different angle.
The scope of the lawsuit is reduced, but Pocketpair versus Nintendo and The Pokémon Company remains an active case within the Tokyo District Court. A preliminary view — which is a first-impression assessment of a subject before all the facts are known or a final decision is made — is planned for November 9 this year.
Palworld hit its 1.0 release in July, netting close to 1 million concurrent players on Steam. In total, Palworld has reached over 40 million players.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Rockstar Games staff will vote on union recognition amid the launch of GTA 6.
item.description:
Rockstar staff will vote on union recognition amid the launch of GTA 6.
Recognition of the IWGB Union at Rockstar will be put to an employee vote from November 12-26, which just so happens to coincide with the release of GTA 6 itself, on November 19.
The terms of the recognition deal were agreed following months of negotiations that took place even as the IWGB and Rockstar clashed over the firing of 31 workers for allegedly leaking company secrets in October last year. The IWGB has alleged the workers were unlawfully fired, and have accused Rockstar Games of union busting. The vote will overlap with the closing submissions of the ongoing employment tribunal, which are set for November 17-18.
Rockstar North and Take-Two Office Protest Photos Nov 2025
The deal would give workers a say over topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies, the IWGB said. Developer Rockstar North, which is part of GTA publisher Rockstar Games, is in Edinburgh, Scotland. If the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union wins the vote, it will become the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry, and, officials said, could boost unionisation efforts across the rest of the industry.
Throughout the process, Rockstar has indicated its willingness to work with staff on union recognition. Rockstar Head of Publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently told Bloomberg: “We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union.”
Rockstar North production co-ordinator and Rockstar Game Workers Union Committee Member Shanti Easton-Steel commented: “This November, we have the chance to make gaming history not once but twice. As all our hard work, skill and creativity are experienced by GTA 6 players for the first time, our voices will now be heard for the first time too.
“For me, this vote comes down to ensuring employees at Rockstar get honesty and openness surrounding the decisions that affect them. When management choices are kept hidden, we can’t properly address issues like the gender pay gap, the uneven and ever-changing policies on overtime pay, or the concerns many co-workers hold around job security post-release.
“This is our moment to secure a window onto the decisions that shape our lives, and a seat at the table to improve them. I’m immensely proud of the games Rockstar gives its fans — I want to be equally proud of the voice Rockstar gives its staff.”
Alex Marshall, President of the IWGB Union, called the vote “just as historic as the game release.”
“But for workers at Rockstar, it is so much more personal: it is fundamentally a choice about whether you get to have a say in how your day-to-day life is organised,” he continued.
“From pay and pensions to parental leave and overtime, this agreement is a real chance to be involved in decision-making at Rockstar by becoming part of a democratic and member-led union.”
Photo by Lesley Martin / AFP via Getty Images.
Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

Last week and over the weekend, one of, if not the, largest board game and tabletop conventions, Spiel Essen, was held in Germany. Board game designers and publishers the world over made their way over to not only demo their games but also reveal brand new upcoming ones. One such game was Blade Runner 2099 from the folks over at Lucky Duck Games which is slated to launch on Kickstarter next year.
Lucky Duck Games, publisher of other such great titles as Unconscious Mind (a game we ranked as one of the best worker placement games you can play right now ) pulled back the cover -literally- of Blade Runner showing off the box during the show over the weekend. Details are still sparse about it but speaking with Lucky Duck, we were able to get a little more information to share. This latest tabletop adventure set in the Blade Runner universe will be a narrative-driven game that you will play alongside a digital app, providing the narration among other features. This time around humans will be the ones being persecuted the game and promises a detective-based cooperative adventure.
Fans of Ridley Scott’s neo-noir science fiction series have a lot to look forward to in the coming year. In addition to Lucky Duck Games’ Blade Runner 2099 Kickstarter campaign launch, a brand new Amazon Prime series is also inbound. Launching in the November, we recently had a chance to sit down and talk with showrunner Silka Luisa about the upcoming “undercover police story”. One thing to note, outside of the name, Lucky Duck’s board game will feature a separate story from that in the Amazon Prime series, though there is no word on whether or not characters may make appearances.
Stay tuned for more details coming in the coming months leading up to the Kickstarter launch next year. Currently, the page is live so head over there and make sure you are notified when it launches.

item.title: Super Smash Bros creator Masahiro Sakurai explained why the boom in AI-created games isn’t likely to create a lasting demand for such projects, comparing them to “low-quality goods” that could never compare to human-made titles like Shadow of the Colossus.
item.description:
Super Smash Bros creator Masahiro Sakurai explained why the boom in AI-created games isn’t likely to create a lasting demand for such projects, comparing them to “low-quality goods” that could never compare to human-made titles like Shadow of the Colossus.
Sakurai made these remarks in an interview with Denfaminico Gamer after he was asked for his thoughts on the huge boom in games that have been released on Steam since 2010. The interviewer noted that, since 2010, this amount skyrocketed from 275 titles to 19,000 titles.
“19,000 is amazing, but I think that number will increase even more from now on. I'm sure of it. That's because AI will increase the number. However, I think most of them will become ‘unprofitable titles.’ There are too many to keep track of, and it's impossible to understand them all,” he said.
“When it comes to things created with AI... or things mass-produced with poor quality, I think most of them will simply be reproductions of systems seen in various other games. I think there are already a lot of those now.”
Photo Mode in Shadow of the Colossus
He went on to mention conceptually simple games that fall into the puzzle genre, even calling out the viral Needle in a Haystack Simulator as part of his example. According to Sakurai, these types of games are easy for AI to recreate, as artificial intelligence cannot make something original, but only iterate on what has come before.
“Titles like, ‘The supermarket has been turned upside down, let's rearrange the products,’ ‘Let's put the screws back in place,’ or ‘Let's find a needle in the haystack’ have become incredibly common. They're also part of the puzzle game genre. I think that kind of imitation should be very easy for AI. However, even if AI can create various works, it's possible that we might see AI creating something similar to the works that Ueda (Fumito) has created — for example, by studying the atmosphere of ICO or Shadow of the Colossus.
“But what Mr. Ueda plans to create in the future is something that AI simply cannot replicate. What kind of artistic style will his future works possess? That's something only he can create. I think that's where human creativity lies. Basically, AI refers to ‘things that have been created so far,’ but it can't refer to ‘things that haven't been created before.’ I think this is true not only for AI, but for various kinds of creative works, as well.”
Sakurai concluded this line of thought by saying that people like Ueda, who “forge their own path” and “can create their own unique flavor," will become "increasingly important from now on," saying this is “especially true in an era of mass production and low-quality goods.”
Sakurai’s remarks couldn’t come at a better time. Over the last few weeks, AI mods have become a wildly popular trend in the gaming space, with players using the technology to port games to web browsers, combine two totally different games into a single experience, and even create ‘new’ games using pre-existing properties. As more and more layoffs hit the industry, and giants like Epic shift to “AI-first” production models, it’s looking grim — but Sakurai’s humanistic vision for a future that prioritizes human-made games with originality and depth paints a brighter picture.
This is the latest news to come from Sakurai after he was forced to abandon his Game Designer Award for the Japan Game Awards when was unable to find a successor to take over his duties after a 16-year-run.
Image Credits: Masahiro Sakurai on Creating Games, YouTube

item.title: The creator of a viral indie game where players must literally find a needle in a haystack is tired of his project getting cloned. So, he made a new game mode, where players must find the real game in a pile of fakes.
item.description:
The creator of a viral indie game where players must literally find a needle in a haystack is tired of his project getting cloned. So, he made a new game mode, where players must find the real game in a pile of fakes.
Thanks to advancements in artificial intelligence, it’s getting easier and easier for players to 'reverse-engineer' video games and even outright copy projects that haven’t been released yet.
It’s been a hellish situation for developers in the industry, particularly for small studios without the funds for legal backing or, even worse, single creators who made their games all by themselves.
NasNakarus is the driving mind behind Needle in a Haystack Simulator, which is exactly what it sounds like. Such a simple concept is easy to copy, and there are currently oodles of similar titles clogging online marketplaces. But he’s not taking it personally; instead, he’s poking fun at the ordeal with some well-timed commentary and a new ‘mode’ for his game.
NasNakarus posted about the mode on October 27, along with a quick demo of what it would look like. In this joke mode, called ‘Find the Original Game,’ players would sift through a pile of game cases with the wording ‘Needle in a Haystack Clone,’ with the ‘Clone’ being in a bright red box. And while players noted that this version of the haystack would be far easier to sort through, it’s less about the mode itself (which may or may not be actually coming to the game), but more about the fact that the developer felt a need to comment on the swath of clones by going to such lengths, at all.
“Our needle in a haystack game has been cloned so many times we made a new game mode,” the dev joked.
Our needle in a haystack game has been cloned so many times we made a new game modefind the original game https://t.co/DH4nBMoYhg
“This is what is called a ‘tragicomedy.’ A situation in which you find yourself, unsure whether to laugh or cry,” one fan replied.
“Someone recreate this on Roblox but you have to search for a specific Roblox game,” another suggested.
Needle in a Haystack Simulator isn’t actually out yet. It’s set to launch in Q4 of 2026, with playtests scheduled for this week. Some users remarked that clones may have taken advantage of this fact, while others pointed out that the concept isn’t exactly a novel one and is, due to its nature, prone to being cloned.
Sony AI NPCs Patent Illustrations
As previously mentioned in this article, the continued evolution of AI is making modding and cloning games easier than ever. Using the technology, modders have been able to port games onto web browsers, combine games (like putting Spider-Man in Batman: Arkham Asylum, for instance), or outright making ‘new’ games based on existing IP. And while some developers are taking legal action against these mods, others — somewhat surprisingly — are speaking out in favor of the trend.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Backrooms director Kane Parsons says he is working on three different "dream projects," which has led to speculation over a collaboration with Valve.
item.description:
Backrooms director Kane Parsons says he is working on three different "dream projects," which has caused no end of speculation regarding a possible collaboration with Valve.
When speaking on The Kyle Buchanan Show, Parsons confirmed he has three "dream projects" currently in the works, all while wearing a Valve hoodie. The young director has made no secret of his love for Valve, particularly Portal and Half-Life.
Earlier this year, Parsons made his big-screen debut with Backrooms, a film adaptation/expansion of his highly popular web horror series. Ever since then, he's been a hot commodity in Hollywood. The filmmaker expressed interest in making a Portal movie around the time of Backrooms' release, which excited fans.
Tomorrow, Kane Parsons comes on The Kyle Buchanan Show to talk about life since the BACKROOMS movie and what he’s working on next. Tune in for the full conversation wherever you watch or listen to podcasts! https://t.co/qu2F31jw1h
Following the release of his debut film, Parsons visited Valve's office, which has led some to believe that he's been actively meeting with the developer to bring their IP to life. This wouldn't be the first try at adapting Valve's franchises, as J.J. Abrams was attempting to bring Half-Life and Portal to the big screen. Abrams said in 2021 that he was still developing Portal, and that a script was being actively worked on. However, no one has heard anything since then.
It's possible Abrams could help produce a Portal film from Parsons, or that Parsons could band together a new creative team. Either way, given the filmmaker's experience and love for Valve's IPs, he'd be a great fit. Whether or not Portal or Half-Life are part of these three "dream projects" remains to be seen, but he did note that they belonged to "powerful forces." He joked that he would be hit with space lasers if he said too much about them, something that doesn't seem as likely if it were an original IP or a continuation of Backrooms.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: In an interview with Yahoo Japan, executive producer Jun Takeuchi outlined Capcom’s plans for its flagship horror franchise, revealing that its encompassing narrative has a definite conclusion — and that end could come shockingly soon.
item.description:
In an interview with Yahoo Japan, executive producer Jun Takeuchi outlined Capcom’s plans for its flagship horror franchise, revealing that its encompassing narrative has a definite conclusion — and that end could come shockingly soon.
Takeuchi began by explaining how the team had expanded on Resident Evil’s overarching story with every game, saying that a ten-year strategy was crafted during the planning stages for Resident Evil 2 Remake.
“The series' story wasn't planned out from the beginning; it expanded with each new game. When we were planning RE:2 and creating a 10-year branding concept, this was the most challenging aspect. If you play through all of them, I think you'll realize the meaning behind the order of the remakes,” he said.
“With the release of Requiem this year, I feel like the first 10 years have come to a close, so I think the conclusion will come in the next 10 years."
Resident Evil Requiem – Performance Screenshots
This is somewhat sad news for hardcore fans who were hoping to blast through hordes of zombies with Leon until the end of time, not to mention fans of all the other characters we’ve come to know and love over the years. And who’s to say if that means we won’t see these characters again in a new, different story?
As for how many Resident Evil games we can expect from Capcom in the interim, Takeuchi assured us that there will be several, though he didn’t describe any of them in depth.
"I can't say, because it would spoil the fun for everyone, but there won't be just one. There will be multiple titles,” he said.
Resident Evil has proven to be a massive hit for Capcom, particularly after RE7: Biohazard shocked life back into the series. Resident Evil 2 Remake is the best-selling game in the franchise, and its most recent addition, Resident Evil Requiem, passed $500 million in revenue after releasing earlier this year, becoming a driving factor in console sales within Japan.
Adding to this, Resident Evil 2 Remake was one of the top ten best-selling titles for Capcom in the first half of its 2027 fiscal year, with RE7 not far behind. Resident Evil 4 was also on that list, as was RE3 and Requiem — meaning that half of the company's top sellers in this period were in the Resident Evil franchise.
There’s lots for Resi fans to look forward to in the coming months; the Code Veronica remake launches early next year, and screenwriter Haris Orkin basically leaked a story mode DLC for Requiem that’s supposed to involve Spencer in some way. There’s also Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie to consider, which was met with rave reviews and a hit at the box office — though it's unlikely Cregger ever makes a sequel, even though he already has plans for what he’d do next.

item.title: Heated Rivalry actor Connor Storrie is in talks to play the villain in Ryan Gosling's Ghost Rider movie.
item.description:
Heated Rivalry actor Connor Storrie is in talks to play the villain in Ryan Gosling's Ghost Rider movie.
According to The Hollywood Reporter, the actor will go toe-to-toe with Gosling's Johnny Blaze. There were some questions over whether or not Gosling would play a different Ghost Rider, but Blaze always made the most sense, and that appears to be the case, per THR's reporting. As of right now, we're not sure which villain Storrie would portray. However, it would be a big leap forward for the actor, who exploded onto the scene earlier this year in the hockey romance series Heated Rivalry.
The actor had also previously starred in Joker: Folie à Deux, as the inmate who fatally stabs Arthur Fleck and is heavily implied to be the "real Joker." Although he had only a couple of minutes of screen time, the role was significant in terms of its impact. Now, it looks like he'll be given a chance to play a real villain in one of the biggest franchises in cinematic history.
Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show
The MCU's Ghost Rider film was confirmed at San Diego Comic-Con this summer, and production has been ramping up rather quickly. The film is expected to begin shooting next year and will target a July 2028 release date. Shawn Levy will direct the film after developing a good relationship with Marvel on Deadpool and Wolverine and Ryan Gosling on his upcoming film Star Wars: Starfighter.
THR also notes that Dune Part 3‘s Linus Sandgren has already been tapped to be the director of photography on the new Ghost Rider movie, and the project will shoot on film. Although this is now a rarity, it's in vogue once again thanks to directors like Christopher Nolan and Ryan Coogler championing the format while successfully getting audiences on board.
Not much else is known about the new Ghost Rider film, but it will be one of the first films post-Avengers: Secret Wars, which should usher in a new era of the MCU. Only time will tell where Johnny Blaze's story will take us, but it sounds like it'll be an exciting prospect.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Acclaimed voice actor and screenwriter David Hayter opened up about his canceled Lost Planet movie adaptation, explaining why it never got off the ground in a throwaway tweet more than a decade after it was first confirmed.
item.description:
Acclaimed voice actor and screenwriter David Hayter opened up about his canceled Lost Planet movie adaptation, explaining why it never got off the ground in a throwaway tweet more than a decade after it was first confirmed.
Did you know that David Hayter, the voice of Solid Snake in the Metal Gear games, wrote the screenplay for a Lost Planet movie? I didn’t either, until he tweeted about it today — almost twenty years after the project fell through.
Hayter spoke up about the film on October 27, 2026, reminding fans that yes, he writes for movies, and one of those movies would have been an absolute dream for fans of Capcom’s long-forgotten sci-fi shooter series Lost Planet.
Fun Fact: I wrote a huge LOST PLANET movie for Warner Brothers in 2008, and then the entire financial world crashed, and that was the end of it.
“Fun Fact: I wrote a huge Lost Planet movie for Warner Brothers in 2008, and then the entire financial world crashed, and that was the end of it,” he wrote.
While Lost Planet’s demise has been thoroughly catalogued at this point — and it’s been so long that newer generations were completely unaware that it even existed, in the first place — this appears to be one of just a few times Hayter has spoken on the 2008 financial crisis playing a part in the project’s premature end.
Previously, Hayter said that internal company politics was to blame, telling MTV in 2010 that there were “some internal issues between a couple of the companies, which I think has caused a delay there.”
E3 2012 Lost Planet 3
And in 2014, Hayter told IGN that the movie — which he described as a “Lawrence of Arabia on an ice planet” — was interrupted by the financial crisis. “Unfortunately, right about the time I was delivering the script, the financial crash hit, and it just devastated the business — in ways that I don't think people grasped. Like, I would get phone calls saying, ‘Well, Disney wants to do such-and-such, but they're out of money until August,’” he explained.
“I heard that about a number of studios. ‘Oh, they're out of money until January,’ or whatever, and I'd never heard that about a movie studio before. So in the midst of all of that turmoil, it just went away, as these things tend to do. So, you know, I guess Warners probably still owns it, and they have my script. I don't know if there are any plans to bring it back up or not. But that was just one of those Hollywood casualties, unfortunately.”
Hayter expounded on some details about his Lost Planet movie in his interview with MTV, saying it “had this incredible visual world. Great suits of armor, great creatures, and its story was about energy — the dwindling energy resources of the Earth and how we’re going to other planets to [solve that problem]. So I thought it was really timely and the world was beautiful. And the other thing that I really felt as a screenwriter made it ideal for adaptation was, the original story in the game was… not… great."
"It was sort of presented in a very Japanese storytelling fashion. It’s very elliptical and difficult to follow, and you’re not really sure who’s who. That’s fine in a game because… you’re really trying to get to the next level. It’s a great opportunity for me as a screenwriter to step in and infuse that incredible visual world with a really compelling — for lack of a better term — American-structured film."
For now, all fans can do is pine after what could have been… though, given Capcom’s renewed interest in “reactivating IPs that haven’t had a new title launch recently," on top of its successful movie adaptations for Resident Evil and Street Fighter, it’s possible that Hayter’s long-awaited Lost Planet flick could come to light. (But maybe that’s just me trying to cope.)

item.title: Curry Barker, writer and director of the brilliantly twisted Obsession, is releasing a new short film on YouTube on October 29.
item.description:
Curry Barker, writer and director of the brilliantly twisted Obsession, is releasing a new short film on YouTube on October 29. The filmmaker shared the news on Instagram along with its title, Mama Bear. The project appears to be part of some sort of Microsoft Windows partnership, but the title suggests something that links to Obsession, rather than an ad for Outlook.
Obsession fans will immediately spot that the title probably relates to the movie's lead character, Baron "Bear" Bailey. We learn early on that he's living in a house he inherited from his grandmother, but his parents are absent from the movie. It makes sense that Barker could explore either Bear's early life or his mother's reaction to the events that happen at the end of the film.
In interviews, Barker has revealed that there's potential for a follow-up to Obsession, telling Deadline:
“I obviously have a couple more things that I’m excited about next, but I do see Obsession 2, maybe. Or even what really is exciting to me is maybe an anthology, like a one-hour episode. Each episode is a different wish that goes completely off the rails. Maybe I’ll direct the pilot with the same DP, and you could invite other filmmakers to kind of give their spin at it. That would be really cool.”
Obsession was a hit in terms of both capitalism and audience reactions. It raked in $520 million worldwide (not bad for a film made on a budget that fell somewhere between $600,000 and $750,000), has already taken home a bunch of awards, and scored high with critics and the public.

item.title: An October 27 statement from employees of Don't Nod, the developer best known for making the original Life is Strange games, warn that the company is in danger of insolvency and layoffs, and accused its management of "illegal" practices that have caused staff "uncertainty and anxiety."
item.description:
An October 27 statement from employees of Don't Nod, the developer best known for making the original Life is Strange games, warn that the company is in danger of insolvency and layoffs, and accused its management of "illegal" practices that have caused staff "uncertainty and anxiety."
The damning statement comes from employees who are members of the French game industry union Le Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu Vidéo, which revealed that Don’t Nod is currently under a safeguard to help protect itself from insolvency (meaning that the company wouldn’t be able to pay its debts).
The statement claims employees were approached by management and given “several financial scenarios” that could happen in the near future, both of which “included redundancies," with the worst case forecasting the “liquidation of the company through 2026.”
Life is Strange: Reunion Screenshots
The message states that “nearly all of the non-managerial jobs” were cut at Don’t Nod, which reportedly included all animators, character artists, concept artists, associate producers, and most environmental artists, sound designers, level designers, programmers, QA testers, HR and developers. Half of its game designers were also laid off, according to the statement.
“Management is extremely clearly going for heavily individualized targeting and hasn’t been shy about their intent to keep selected people in rather than jobs, which is illegal,” the union wrote.
The statement goes on to claim that management is betting on outsourcing to take on the workload of these fired team members — a decision that the union feels is “out-of-touch.”
The letter then says Don't Nod employees have been “living on the edge, in uncertainty and anxiety” for the last two years, to the point where six workplace accidents occurred this year and an inquiry was recently launched into a “serious and immediate danger.” It also alleges that management “refused to let those who would be willing to leave earlier go through a voluntary leave plan,” saying they “do not care about the damage it deals to employees’ health.”
The statement ends on a striking note; a government agency that represents employees is set to make its ruling on November 3. After that, management will have 21 days to decide on a plan. If this plan is accepted by the government agency, it’s possible that employees could “get their firing letters on November 25.”
“If it were to be rejected however, management would have to go back to the drawing board and improvise because, as you might have gathered, planning for contingencies isn’t their forte,” the letter concludes.
This is the latest news to surface regarding Don’t Nod’s dire financial straits after it was warned by auditors in a financial report that it could run out of cash as early as November. Its latest game, Aphelion, was released earlier this year to middling reviews, and given this recent union tell-all, its next project could be in peril.

item.title: A few new details on the story for A24’s Elden Ring movie have emerged, including its possible runtime. And, if that remains the case, it’s going to be epic.
item.description:
A few new details on the story for A24’s Elden Ring movie have emerged, including its possible runtime. And, if that remains the case, it’s going to be epic.
Deadline reports that writer-director Alex Garland’s screenplay, based on FromSoftware’s acclaimed fantasy video game, “runs to at least 180 pages with visuals, implying the movie could push towards three hours. While plot details are largely being kept under wraps, we understand that in-demand Heartstopper actor [Kit] Connor is the protagonist and the ‘faithful’ film will follow his journey. There are said to be battles between his character and impressive monsters and dragons.”
The site also claims that A24 is allowing potential international buyers to read Garland’s Elden Ring script, but only with a studio staff member present (for security reasons, naturally).
It was reported last week that the Elden Ring movie is the most expensive film A24 has ever produced – Deadline’s report today pegs it at “between $175 million-200 million, but closer to the latter” – and now comes word that the studio, which fully financed the film, is looking to mitigate some of that risk by bringing in a partner with very deep pockets: Amazon.
According to Deadline, Amazon MGM Studios has now acquired “a bunch of international pay-1 streaming rights... The pact is understood to cover a large number of international markets, and sources speculate to us that it is easily worth tens of millions of dollars. We hear the deal could also potentially lead to interesting activations on Amazon’s Twitch platform.”
The film’s huge price tag makes Elden Ring one of the most expensive films that will be shopped at next month’s American Film Market, which touts itself as “the premier marketplace for the acquisition, development, financing, and distribution of independent film, television, and premium content for audiences worldwide.”
Potential buyers at AFM will reportedly be treated to an Elden Ring movie presentation of some kind, including possibly seeing the very first footage from this highly-anticipated film.
Upcoming New Video Game Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond
After some set photos made their way online, Elden Ring wrapped filming in July and is scheduled to open in theaters on March 3, 2028.
In addition to Kit O’Connor, the cast includes Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, Nick Offerman and Peter Serafinowicz.
Are you excited by the prospect of a three-hour Elden Ring movie? Let us know in the comments.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.
